Fit a different model to the same data

Source: R/fit.R
update.baysesp_fit.Rd

Fits a new model to the data of a model already fitted with baysesp(), with the same backend and the same sampling settings (number of chains, warmup and sampling iterations, seed, and the further arguments given to baysesp()). Only the model changes: its class, its priors or its verification mechanism. This is the usual way to fit the alternative models given to compare_models().

Usage

# S3 method for class 'baysesp_fit'
update(object, model = object@model, ...)

Arguments

object

A model fitted with baysesp().

model

The new model: an object created by saturated(), loglinear() or random_effects(), with its priors and its verification mechanism (verification = mar() or verification = mnar()). Default object@model, the model of object, which fits the same model again.

...

Sampling settings that replace those of object, with the names of the arguments of baysesp(): backend, chains, iter_warmup, iter_sampling, seed, or arguments for the backend such as cores. Settings that are not given are those used for object; the seed, if object was fitted with seed = NULL, is the one drawn at that time.

Value

A new baysesp_fit object, as returned by baysesp().

See also

baysesp(), compare_models()

Examples

# \donttest{
set.seed(1)
d <- simulate_study(n = 1000, prevalence = 0.2,
                    sensitivity = c(A = 0.9, B = 0.8),
                    specificity = c(A = 0.85, B = 0.95),
                    verification_prob = c(0.2, 0.9, 0.9, 1))
d <- baysesp_data(d, tests = c("A", "B"), verified = "verified", disease = "disease")
fit <- baysesp(d, seed = 1)
fit_ci <- update(fit, model = loglinear(interaction_order = 1))
fit_ci
#> <baysesp_fit> loglinear model, MAR verification, 4 chains x 1000 draws (rstan)
